assessment.summary: CD274 (PD-L1) is a highly validated immuno-oncology target with exceptional structural, chemical, and clinical evidence. Five approved antibody drugs exist, over 1,700 ChEMBL IC50 entries are recorded, and 80 PDB structures including sub-angstrom resolution co-crystal structures confirm a well-characterised binding interface. Druggability is high, though the dominant modality remains biologics; small-molecule inhibitors of the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction are an active but more challenging area.
evidence_gaps: Small-molecule druggability of the PD-1/PD-L1 protein-protein interface remains challenging; approved drugs are all monoclonal antibodies, not small molecules
Oral bioavailability and pharmacokinetic profiles of small-molecule PD-L1 inhibitors are not well established in the clinic
Resistance mechanisms to PD-L1 blockade (e.g., CD274 amplification, alternative immune checkpoints) are incompletely characterised and may limit therapeutic durability
Structural data predominantly covers the extracellular IgV domain; intracellular domain structure and signalling function are less well characterised
Biomarker strategies for patient selection beyond IHC-based PD-L1 expression scoring remain an open question
